Book correction: The 'Point to Note' box beside Question 16 says \left|\frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1}\right| = \frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1} > 1 for x \in (-\infty, -1) \cup (1, \infty) (true) and that \frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1} < -1 has no solution. The second statement is wrong: for 0 < |x| < 1 the denominator is negative, e.g. x = \frac{1}{2} gives \frac{5/4}{-3/4} = -\frac{5}{3} < -1. In fact \frac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1} \leq -1 f
